name: Beechcraft Skipper (77)
summary: Beechcraft's side-by-side two-seat, T-tailed trainer of 1979–82, with the Musketeer's construction methods and a spin-resistant-by-design GA(W)-1 wing.

wings: Wing mounted low on the fuselage
engines: Single Lycoming flat-four in a short cowl
tail: T-tail with the stabilator atop the fin

tellTales: T-tail on a small low-wing two-seater
Fixed tricycle gear with a short cowl
Trainer-sized fuselage with a high horizontal tail

confusedWith.howToTell: Both have T-tails; the Skipper's cabin looks more conventional with less bubble-like glass, while the Tomahawk's is a rounded greenhouse.
The Skipper is a low-wing with a T-tail; the 150 is a high-wing with a conventional tail.
The Skipper is a smaller two-seater with a T-tail; the Musketeer is a four-seater with a low-set horizontal tail.
The Skipper is a framed metal aircraft with a T-tail; the DA20 is a composite with a clear bubble canopy and a conventional tail.
